Subject: Pricing annex: bucket syndication and amortization proposal

Lena / ACME procurement team,

Thanks again for the call last week. Per our discussion I attached a short mark-up of the pricing exhibit and a tracked copy with a few structural edits (pricing_exhibit_marissa_v4.pdf; redlines_annotated.docx). The key points we changed are intended to keep the economic intent intact while addressing your legal team's requests. TL;DR of the proposed compromises we think will get this over the line: 

- Bucket syndication: allow credits to apply across product SKUs within the same order schedule subject to a quarterly cross-usage cap of 20% to preserve SKU-level economics.
- Amortization of credits: we propose 12 months amortization on any upfront true-up credit (rather than a multi-year hold) but with a 6-month true-up cadence to reconcile usage early.
- Escrow carve: if ACME prefers extended amortization, we are open to holding 20% of the committed fee in escrow for 12 months instead of stretching amortization out to 36 months.
- Waterfall language: removed the "automatic waterfall" language and replaced with explicit priority order (billing > overage credits > true-up) so it's operationally deterministic.

Please have your procurement/legal review the attached redlines and call out any absolute blockers. If you can share ACME's annotated PDF, I can escalate internally to legal and finance for one last pass. I can also set up a quick 30-minute sync if helpful.

Next step: would love to close on the exhibit markup this week so we can route to DocuSign before EOM.

Attachments: pricing_exhibit_marissa_v4.pdf (annotated), redlines_annotated.docx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Marissa —

Thanks for the markup and the clear summary. Our legal team reviewed and attached ACME's comments (ACME_redline_v2.pdf). A couple of substantive asks from our side: 

1) Amortization length — our CFO/legal are uncomfortable with a 12-month amortization for larger credits tied to a multi-product bundle. They asked if Redwood will accept 24 months as a compromise (they're pushing hard on that because of revenue recognition and internal reporting).

2) Frequency of true-ups — we can accept quarterly true-ups but they want an explicit clause that any adjustments >10% in a quarter trigger a pro-rata recalculation in the next invoice cycle (to avoid lagged exposure).

3) Cross-sku application — we are okay with cross-usage but cannot accept a hard 20% cap per quarter across the entire order schedule; instead, we'd like SKU-level watermarks so that high-volume SKUs don't get starved.

4) Escrow — ACME legal prefers not to set an escrow account unless absolutely necessary. If Redwood needs protection, can you explain why escrow is preferable to a longer amortization from your perspective?

We do not view the water-fall language as a deal-breaker, but your proposed priority order needs to be explicit about invoice timing and dispute holdbacks.

I'm looping procurement and legal to this thread. Attaching our redline so your team can work from that. Happy to schedule a 30-minute legal vs legal call if that helps sort precise language.

Best,
Lena Park
Head of Procurement, ACME Cloud
lena.park@acmecloud.com | +1 212-555-0198

Folks — forwarding ACME's redline and Lena's notes. Quick internal recommendation for a signable compromise so we stop oscillating: 

- Offer: 18-month amortization for upfront credits on multi-product bundles (split the difference between 12 and 24).
- True-up cadence: keep quarterly true-ups; add a clause that adjustments >15% in a quarter will be pro-rated into the subsequent invoice (compromise on their 10%).
- Cross-sku cap: convert to per-SKU watermark rather than a hard global cap: allow 20% cross-usage per SKU, but allow finance to request a temporary waiver for a single SKU if there's a product migration event (e.g., legacy SKU deprecation).
- Escrow: propose escrow as an option if ACME insists on amortization >18 months; escrow amount = 20% of committed fee held for 12 months, with quarterly release tied to usage reconciliation. 

Why this makes sense operationally: 18 months shortens revenue recognition impact relative to 24–36 months while giving ACME some runway to settle large credits; the pro-rate threshold reduces jitter for both sides; SKU watermarking preserves SKU economics but is operationally simpler than per-line-item caps.

If legal (Laura) and finance (Karthik) are OK with language, I'll send a clean marked-up PDF and request ACME's legal to sign. If you want to tighten any definitions ("committed fee", "true-up event"), call them out and I can lock definitions into the exhibit.

Marissa

Lena / ACME team —

Thanks for the constructive feedback. Per Marissa's internal note, Redwood legal and finance conferred and we believe the package below is a practical middle ground. Attached is the proposed redline (rwdw_acme_markedup_exhibit_20281009.pdf) reflecting the agreed compromises: 

- 18-month amortization for upfront credits on multi-product bundles.
- Quarterly true-ups with a 15% trigger for pro-rata invoice adjustment.
- Per-SKU watermark for cross-sku credit application (20% cap per SKU) with a one-time waiver clause for SKU migration upon written notice.
- Escrow only applies if ACME requests amortization beyond 18 months; escrow equal to 20% of committed fee, held for 12 months, with quarterly releases tied to reconciliations.
- Explicit invoice priority language included; disputes may hold up amounts under formal dispute but do not delay recognized credits for uncontroverted amounts.
